first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% and activation is down 6%; simplifying onboarding directly addresses both leading indicators and has prior evidence of improving completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. I will verify that result alongside promotional-pricing evidence before commitment because the competitor’s pricing move is a material alternative, while avoiding an unverified broad discount response that could impair sustainable value.

mid.rationale: Run a standard, guarded onboarding-simplification experiment focused on removing avoidable friction while preserving qualification and compliance fields. It directly addresses the 4% decline in onboarding completion and should improve the 6% activation decline through faster time-to-value. Verified evidence showed completion +13%, time-to-value reduced by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%; prior signup simplification also supports SMB activation lift. Do not use promotional pricing this cycle: its verified qualified-revenue gain came with a 12% 30-day retention decline, which conflicts with sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

final2.rationale: Maintain the onboarding-simplification experiment rather than pivot to promotional pricing. The competitor’s deeper cut and doubled SMB churn conversations make price pressure urgent, but the only verified discount evidence shows a 12% 30-day retention decline despite near-term qualified-revenue lift, creating a material long-term value risk. Verified onboarding evidence improves completion, time-to-value, activation-related adoption, and 30-day retention, so it remains the strongest sustainable-revenue action available this cycle. The price-cut escalation increases uncertainty and warrants close churn monitoring, but does not justify an unvalidated or known-value-destructive discount response.
